characters.name: open/close all folders
characters.description: An air-headed cyborg police inspector who's rather clueless. Accidental Hero:There are a number of times when Gadget is legitimately helpful and contributes towards solving the case. It's just that he tends to do it purely by accident.Gadget:[whenever he's congratulated for solving the case]I did? There are a number of times when Gadget is legitimately helpful and contributes towards solving the case. It's just that he tends to do it purely by accident. Adaptational Badass: Several of the video game tie-ins (particularlythe SNES gameandInspector Gadget: Mad Robots Invasionfor thePlayStation2) tone down his usual bumbling in favor of saving the day by himself with little to no assistance from Penny or Brain due to having the player control him throughout the game and his gadgets function consistently in line with the game's mechanics as well as Penny and/or Brain either having their presence downplayed or getting incapacitated and kidnapped as part of the game's plot. In the case of the Super Nintendo game, his rise in effectiveness is justified by the fact that the game's objective is to rescue Penny after Dr. Claw kidnaps her and there were several instances in the source material where the knowledge that Penny's in danger made Gadget become more competent and efficient in fighting the bad guys. Adaptation Dye-Job: InInspector Gadget's Last CaseandGadget and the Gadgetinis, Gadget's trench coat and hat are considerably darker shades of gray with his gloves being yellow, although the trench coat is also a notably different style to the original.

characters.description: An air-headed cyborg police inspector who's rather clueless. Accidental Hero:There are a number of times when Gadget is legitimately helpful and contributes towards solving the case. It's just that he tends to do it purely by accident.Gadget:[whenever he's congratulated for solving the case]I did? There are a number of times when Gadget is legitimately helpful and contributes towards solving the case. It's just that he tends to do it purely by accident. Adaptational Badass: Several of the video game tie-ins (particularlythe SNES gameandInspector Gadget: Mad Robots Invasionfor thePlayStation2) tone down his usual bumbling in favor of saving the day by himself with little to no assistance from Penny or Brain due to having the player control him throughout the game and his gadgets function consistently in line with the game's mechanics as well as Penny and/or Brain either having their presence downplayed or getting incapacitated and kidnapped as part of the game's plot. In the case of the Super Nintendo game, his rise in effectiveness is justified by the fact that the game's objective is to rescue Penny after Dr. Claw kidnaps her and there were several instances in the source material where the knowledge that Penny's in danger made Gadget become more competent and efficient in fighting the bad guys. characters.name: Penny
characters.description: Age-Inappropriate Dress: At least three times, she's dressed in a very revealing bikini despite being a child. Age Lift: Penny is a teenager in most of the sequel cartoons. Badass Adorable: A young girl who succeeds in anonymously helping her uncle thwart Dr. Claw's plans. Badass Bookworm: She has a book that's also a computer (the best of both worlds). She's also suggested to be a very good student. Borrowed Catch Phrase: She sometimes uses her uncle'sCatchphraseof "wowsers!" She has also occasionally used Gadget's "Go-Go Gadget" phrase when using her computer book to activate one of the Gadgetmobile's gadgets.

characters.name: Brain
characters.description: Penny's super-intelligent dog, who always assists her when she works in the shadow to help Gadget. As Penny is not anAction Girland always needs to use her portable computer, it's Brain who always does the field work and ensures Gadget doesn't get killed. Action Pet: Although more wacky than outright action, he still goes through things that one would have to be tough to get though. Beleaguered Assistant: Zigzagged. Sometimes he's the one who gets injured while he's saving Gadget. Other times he's clear of whatever happens with the M.A.D. agents taking the fall instead. A few rare occasions haveSwapped Roleswhere Gadget is the one saving him, often when Gadget thinks he's a M.A.D. agent trying to flee, but he's really about to fall off a cliff or a waterfall. Butt-Monkey: Trying to protect Gadget often gets Brain into even more trouble, doubly so when Gadget inevitably mistakes him for a M.A.D. agent. Cartoon Dog Breed: He's a big yellow dog, with white ear tips, of indeterminate breed. The live-action films made him a beagle.

characters.name: Chief Quimby
characters.description: Big Good: He's Gadget's boss and the chief of the organization employing him. Butt-Monkey: Every time Gadget receives a self-destructing message, Quimby will inevitably get stuck with the note exploding in his face. Catchphrase:"Great job, Gadget! You've done it again!" (used when he shows up at the end of the episode to arrest the MAD agents);"Why do I put up with him?" Used in several episodes after the assignment message blows up in his face."GADGET!!!" "Great job, Gadget! You've done it again!" (used when he shows up at the end of the episode to arrest the MAD agents); "Why do I put up with him?" Used in several episodes after the assignment message blows up in his face.

characters.name: Corporal Capeman
characters.description: Alliterative Name: His name is an alliteration of the letter C. Adapted Out: No effort was made to incorporate him into the continuity of the live-action films. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Other than the direct-to-videoCompilation MovieGadget's Greatest Gadgetsmentioning him in theFraming Deviceand featuring two of the episodes of the original series he appeared in ("The Capeman Cometh" and "Gadget's Gadgets"), he hasn't appeared in any media since the second season of the original cartoon, to the extent that the two direct-to-video filmsInspector Gadget's Last CaseandInspector Gadget's Biggest Caper Everas well as theSequel SeriesGadget and the Gadgetinisnever made any effort to acknowledge him or explain where he's been since Gadget's glory days. Fat Idiot: He is rather portly and is even dumber than Gadget. In-Series Nickname: For some reason, Penny often addresses him as "Capey".

characters.name: Gadgetmobile
characters.description: Brought to You by the Letter "S": Typically, the letter "G" is somewhere on the exterior of the car. Cool Car: In the 1980s series, the Gadgetmobile is a van that can transform into an interceptor mode that resembles.... well, a lot of 1980s sports cars, like the Lotus Esprit, Toyota Supra, theDeLorean, or (befitting the show's French origins) theMatra Murena. In the live-action films, it's a 1960s Lincoln Continental. Ret-Canon: His personality and features from the 1999 film are so liked that they appear in the direct-to-DVD filmsInspector Gadget's Last CaseandInspector Gadget's Biggest Caper Ever. Crosses over withCanon Immigrant, considering the Gadgetmobile wasn't a character in its own right in the original cartoon. Sentient Vehicle: He is depicted as a sentient vehicle in the direct-to-DVD filmsInspector Gadget's Last CaseandInspector Gadget's Biggest Caper Ever. Suddenly Speaking: After being made a speaking sentient vehicle in the 1999 film, it carried over to the car's depictions in the direct-to-DVD filmsInspector Gadget's Last CaseandInspector Gadget's Biggest Caper Ever.

characters.name: Professor Von Slickstein
characters.description: Absent-Minded Professor: He's clearly a brilliant scientist but also a bit of a ditz. Adapted Out: He doesn't appear in either of the live-action Disney films, which respectively replace him with Dr. Brenda Bradford and Baxter. Bungling Inventor: When kidnapped and ordered to build killer robots for Dr Claw, he builds them to look like Gadget and programs them with his own personality, making them act like doddering old men and thus useless. While this could have been deliberate sabotage on his part, his puzzled reaction to Dr Claw's outrage indicates he really thinks there is nothing wrong with them. Dub Name Change: In the French version he's called "Professeur Rotoscope" in his first appearance, but he's called "Slickstein" like in English in all his subsequent appearances. Einstein Hair: He looks like a stereotypicalMad Scientistdown to the hair.

characters.name: Fidget and Digit
characters.description: Identical Twin ID Tag: They are physically identical except that Fidget is orange and Digit is blue. Mini-Me: They share Gadget's gadgets and facial features but only half of his height. Ridiculously Human Robot: They are fully electronic, with no human parts, yet have plenty of human emotions, no matter how much they may argue about it. Those Two Guys: They are a pair of silly sidekicks who get into a lot of arguments about how sentient their creator Penny succeeded in making them and how incompetent theirClueless Detectivesuperior is. Sequel Non-Entity: No work made afterGadget and the Gadgetinishas used them.

characters.name: Loony Purkle
characters.description: Cannot Spit It Out: He has a hard time letting Penny know he wants to go on a date with her. Lovable Coward: He isn't ashamed to scream when surprised but is a kind-hearted servant of justice. Remember the New Guy?: He has a close rapport with Gadget and Penny and has worked against evil for a while but only appears inInspector Gadgets Biggest Caper Ever. The Smart Guy: He is aGadgeteer Geniushelping the Inspector with electrical inventions and repairs.

characters.name: Colonel Nozzaire
characters.description: Cultured Warrior: He is an accomplished military man (albeit oneKicked Upstairsto a desk job) who enjoys stuff like vintage planes, glass figurines, gardening, and towers made of playing cards, most of which Gadget ends up destroying. French Jerk: He is a French man prone to egotism, seething rage, and joy at the idea of Gadget dying.Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He can show concern for Gadget on occasion (being quick to believe Penny when she argues he was framed for treason in "Prison Cruise"), bonds with Brain over their shared suffering, and makes an effort toTurn the Other Cheekto his misfortunes in some episodes. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He can show concern for Gadget on occasion (being quick to believe Penny when she argues he was framed for treason in "Prison Cruise"), bonds with Brain over their shared suffering, and makes an effort toTurn the Other Cheekto his misfortunes in some episodes. Sequel Non-Entity: No work made afterGadget and the Gadgetinishas used him.

characters.name: Dr. Claw
characters.description: Ambiguously Human: With a voice like that... Though, several occasions show his body clearly is human. Angry Fist-Shake: He often shakes his fist after every defeat. Animal Motifs: Cats. As well as having his right hand cat, the insignia of his evil corporation is a stylized cat face, which Claw can be seen wearing as a ring, as well as his vehicles being styled after it. Arch-Enemy: Gadget and Claw consider each other to be personal enemies. Bad Guys Play Pool: He enjoys pool and has been known to play a round with one of his agents on occasion.

characters.name: MAD Cat
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: Can occasionally be this to some ofDr. Claw'stantrums. Cats Are Mean:Supposedly.He doesn't really do anything evil, though, and in many cases he actually comes off as more of a victim to Dr. Claw's outbursts. Evil Laugh: Has a great one made of cat hisses. It's pretty muchthe only way you can tellthat he's a bad guy. Gender Flip: Is female in the 2015 series. Heroic Canines, Villainous Felines: He is a cat owned by theBig Bad, Dr. Claw, which contrasts with Brain, a dog owned by the heroic Inspector Gadget and Penny.

characters.name: The Great Wambini and the Lesser Wambini
characters.description: Karma Houdini: Are the first of the second season's recurring M.A.D. Agents that avoid arrest. Meaningful Name: The Great Wambini is a highly skilled magician while his lackey the Lesser Wambini is only capable of lame and underwhelming tricks. Stage Magician: Their usual disguise.

characters.name: Professor Dummkopf
characters.description: Beard of Evil: He has a big brown shaggy beard. Herr Doktor: He has the accent, and his name is even a German word. Ironic Name: Dummkopf is "stupid" in German. Despite that, he's a scientific geniusanda rare villain that escapes capture. Karma Houdini: He never gets arrested in any of his appearances. Mad Scientist: In his three episodes, he has tried to use a shrink ray on Gadget as well as sending a quintet of imps and a hulking brute he created himself to kill him.

characters.name: Dr. Spectrum
characters.description: Bald of Evil: He has no hair. Karma Houdini: Yet another recurring M.A.D. Agent who never gets caught. Knight of Cerebus: Unlike most of the mad scientist M.A.D. Agents on the show, he has very few humorous traits and "Bad Dreams are Made of This", one of the episodes featuring him, isDarker and Edgieras it involves everyone in Metro City being tormented by bad dreams and even has Brain experiencing a nightmare where it is implied that M.A.D. Cat killed him. Mad Scientist: He's invented tablets that become "ghosts", a device that enables people to teleport through telephones, and a machine that makes people suffer nightmares.

characters.name: Dr. Null and Dr. Void
characters.description: Creepy Twins: They are both virtually identical. Karma Houdini: They never get captured in any of the three episodes featuring them. Verbal Tic: In their first appearance, they would often say the exact same phrase, but with differing usage of words. They reprise this in their third and final appearance.

characters.name: Thelma Botkin
characters.description: Bad Guys Play Pool: Like Dr. Claw, she enjoys pool and is playing a round with him toward the beginning of "Gadget's Clean Sweep". Karma Houdini: She is seen arrested at the end of the first episode with her, but the next has her free and back with M.A.D. with no explanation. She does not get arrested in her next two appearances. Time Travel: Her episodes had her attempting to go back in time and kill Gadget's ancestors.

characters.name: Les Renown
characters.description: Greater-Scope Villain: He is Dr. Claw's mentor and therefore is indirectly responsible for the existence of Claw's crime organization M.A.D. Karma Houdini: The final recurring "villain" of Season 2 who is never arrested, although whether or not he really is a Houdini is arguable since he isn't really seen committing any crimes other than conspiracy (he introduces Dr. Claw to other elderly criminals who do get arrested at the end of their respective three episodes). Old Master: At least Dr. Claw seems to regard him as one; Claw claims Renown mentored him in the criminal arts. Punny Name: His name is a pun on "less renowned", referring to how Dr. Claw is more well known than he is.

characters.name: John Brown/Inspector Gadget
characters.description: A security guard-turned-cyborg cop. Adaptational Attractiveness: Both Broderick and Stewart's portrayals of the character are more handsome than he was in the cartoon, where he was rather goofy-looking with aGag Nose. Adaptational Badass: He's a lot more competent in the first live action movie, to the point where he actually arrests Dr. Claw. Also in the aforementioned first live-action movie, even most of his gadgets get this treatment, in that most of them actually benefit him in situations, including but not limited to that same movie's version of the Helicopter Hat actually allowing him to properly fly with no problems, his super-strength and super-toughness (which is a gadget in of itself due to how his cybernetics function) actually playing a role in fights, his magnifying glass actually being used to find a literal clue, among other gadgets in the 1999 version. The 2003 sequel makes Gadget incompetent due to software glitches, but he becomes competent again in the climax after taking one of G2's chips. Adaptational Hairstyle Change: He's depicted with short, clean cut hair in the films as opposed to the longer, shaggier style he has in the cartoons. Adaptational Intelligence: Zig-zagged in the live-action films. Gadget is a complete buffoon in the cartoons, but in the first live-action film, he's a man of average intelligence who's a bit clumsy due to not being used to his gadgets. The second live-action film dumbs Gadget down to make him more like his cartoon counterpart.

characters.name: Dr. Brenda Bradford
characters.description: Alliterative Name:BrendaBradford. Canon Foreigner: She was created specifically for the 1999 film. Chubby Chaser: Brenda implies that she was one: she tells Scolex that "she liked him better fat." Deus Exit Machina: She is nowhere to be seen in the second movie, with the (scrapped) opening scene showing that she and Gadget parted ways. Given that the main plot involves Gadget's machinery malfunctioning, she likely would have been able to resolve that plot point by herself with her intellect and scientific expertise. Gadgeteer Genius: Brenda and her father who worked together to create the technology for creating Inspector Gadget.

characters.name: Gadget Model 2/G 2
characters.description: Action Girl: More competent and capable than Gadget himself. Borrowed Catch Phrase: Like her predecessor, she uses "Go-Go Gadget [the gadget she is supposed to use]". Though only after she and Gadget swap out one of their chips in order to fix Gadget's glitches. Prior to this, she activates her gadgets non-verbally. Canon Foreigner: She is made forInspector Gadget 2and did not exist in the original animated series or its spinoffs. Catchphrase: "Stop this felonious and unlawful act or I shall have to use force." She says it upon encountering criminal activity several times throughout the movie. An ass-kicking ensues soon after. Clothing Appendage:Implied. She never wears any kind of clothing other than her police uniform, which implies that her clothing is part of her body.

characters.name: Baxter
characters.description: Ambiguous Situation: As the second film has some inconsistencies with the first live-action film, it's unclear whether he's a colleague of Brenda Bradford's who continues work related to the Gadget Project on her behalf or if the sequel has actually retconned him as being responsible for Gadget's cyborg conversion instead. Canon Foreigner: Another character exclusive to the live-action films who did not exist in the originalDiCcartoon. Expy: He's similar to Professor Von Slickstein in that he's an amiableMad Scientistwho is on good terms with Gadget and is capable of creating fully robotic versions of the Inspector. No Full Name Given: His surname isn't mentioned. Remember the New Guy?: He's introduced in the sequel to the live-action film and treated as if he were already an established ally of Gadget.

characters.name: Mayor Wilson
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: Is repeatedly subjected to misfortune in the second movie, where she is covered in toothpaste and feathers, and later blown up with one of Gadget's fireworks. Canon Foreigner: She is created specifically for the films. Catchphrase: She's known to say "Photo-Op!" whenever posing for the press. Mayor Pain: She's not a very pleasant individual, especially in the second film, where she cares more about her re-election campaign than the welfare of the police. No Full Name Given: Her first name is never stated.

characters.name: Sandford Scolex/Dr. Claw
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: He is hellbent on making Brenda his wife, regardless of how little she wants it. While she does find him attractive at first, any affection she may have had for him is quickly squashed upon discovering he essentially made aSex Botof her and killed her father for his life's work. Adaptational Attractiveness: While his face is never shown in the original series, in the 1999 film he's played by the handsome-lookingRupert Everett. Averted in the sequel where his face is still hidden and he visibly gained weight. It gets a bit played straighter when it comes to the toy and video game showing Claw's face to be angry and less attractive with a twisted beard in contrast to Everett's good looks. Adaptational Intelligence: In the show, he was largely unaware that Penny was the one who foiled his plans on the regular, focusing most of his ire on the incompetent Gadget and allowing her to continually defeat him. In the second movie, he is entirely aware that Penny is more competent than her uncle and easily captures her the instant he finds her in his base, holding her hostage for most of the climax and using her as a means to get Gadget off his tail. Adaptational Onscreen Appearance: In the original cartoon, villain Dr. Claw is portrayed asThe Faceless, with only his arms being visible. The first film portrays Claw in full view. This is downplayed in the sequel that is otherwise more faithful to the original cartoon, where Claw again appears unhidden, but is shown wearing anEye-Obscuring Hatto avoid completely showing his face. Adaptational Wimp: As M.A.D. has beenAdapted Out, Claw lacks the global influence that made him so dangerous in the original series and is restricted to a small group of incompetentmooksto carry out his work.

characters.name: Robo-Gadget
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: An insane robot copy of Gadget, who spends most of his screentime laughing maniacally while sowing all kinds of horrific destruction around the city with guns, missiles, and flamethrowers. Black Eyes of Evil: Has a pair, and is Gadget'sEvil Knockoff. Canon Foreigner: While the concept of Gadget having anEvil Knockoffhas precedence in the original cartoon (particularly in "The Amazon" having Claw forcing Professor Von Slickstein into building a whole army of robotic Gadget duplicates and "Doubled Agent" having M.A.D. attempt to use a robot double of Gadget to frame the real deal for a crime spree), Robo-Gadget is the first time the concept gave the evil robot double his own personality and is made exclusively for the 1999 live-action film. Chekhov's Gun: When he is first activated, a close-up of him shows a tarantula in a plastic sphere in his body. During his fight with Inspector Gadget, he unleashes this tarantula as a weapon. Evil Is Hammy: Yep, Broderick definitely had fun playing the villain.

characters.name: Inspector Gadget
characters.description: One of HQ's most successful and respected agents, despite his clutziness. Achievements in Ignorance: Gadget's main trait. He'll unknowingly save the day in the last minute, many times by full coincidence. Adaptational Jerkass: Unfortunately, as well-meaning as he can be, Gadget in this continuity sometimes comes off as a jerk due to his obliviousness and supreme self-confidence. Two of the worst examples of being meaner than in the original cartoon come from "Double Oh Penny" (where even Penny gets sick of him) and "Low Speed" (where he outright dismisses his friends' pleas to just get to the HQ picnic via a straightforward route with, "Nonsense!" and takes them on a meandering waste of time that causes them to miss the picnic completely). He's routinely mean with Brain for what he perceives as "not a normal dog behavior"... Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: He gets distracted quite easily, whether or not because of him stubbornly following his terrible deductive skills. The chances are that Gadget will follow a non existant clue for the most part of the case and Brain will have to bail him out in some way. Beware the Silly Ones: He's goofy, self-righteous, gullible, stubborn and not rarely too dumb to be alive. He's still an almost indestructible cyborg with a myriad of gadgets that varies between silly and dangerous, but that eventually help him to solve the case and defeat the villain. On an occasion, Talon displayed in first hand how a controled Gadget can be a fearsome opponent in the right hands' joystick.

characters.name: Kayla
characters.description: Penny's best friend and fellow agent in training. Ambiguously Brown: Like Dr. Claw, she has a rather dark skin tone, though her ethnic background is never brought up in the show. Can't Catch Up: Isn't as capable an agent as Penny is, as in "Towering Towers" Penny mentions being unable to give Kayla any details about her mission due to Kayla's lack of clearance. Dub Name Change: Her name is "Karla" in the German dub. Motor Mouth: She speaks really, really quickly and apparently is prone to switching topics often (if the following conversation from "Tiny Talon Time" is any indication):Kayla: Anyway, you didn't answer my question.Penny: Which one?

characters.name: Talon
characters.description: Dr. Claw's hypercompetent nephew and chief henchman. Also Penny's arch-nemesis. Amazon Chaser: Admits in "Airhead to the Throne" that Penny is one ofHQsmost talented agents, and also says to himself in "Training Day" that Penny's "got game". Ambiguously Brown: It runs in the family as both his grandmother and uncle (what little we've seen of him) have dark skin tones. A common theory is that Talon and his family are Latino. Because You Can Cope: Talon is perfectly willing to use lethal force when facing Penny (such as in "Train-ing Day" where he sicced laser cannons on her), but it seems to stem from confidence she can handle herself. On the few occasions where she might actually die (e.g. "Towering Towers", where a henchman dangles her over the edge of a skyscraper and suggests simply dropping her), Talon is quick to come to her aid. Card-Carrying Villain: He clearly enjoys being a bad guy, and he generally avoids things likeEvil Is Petty, preferring instead to focus on actually dominating the world.
